summary: Kitaro Nishida was a philosopher and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Karl Florenz. He held posts at the Fourth Higher School (1899–1909) and served as professor of philosophy at Kyoto University (1910–1928).

Kiyoaki Okuda is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his doctoral studies under Ludwig Alsdorf around 1968–1973. He served as a professor at Shitennoji University from roughly 1975 to 2008 and directed the Shitennoji Doctrinal Research Institute.

Kiyoshi Kato was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his BA at Otani University, where he studied under Enga Teramoto, and later worked at Higashi Honganji in 1935 and Hyangsam Vocational Girls' School in 1938.

Kiyoshi Miki was a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University under Kitaro Nishida from roughly 1917 to 1920. He subsequently held academic posts at Otani University and Ryukoku University around 1925 to 1927.

Kiyoshi Okano is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Bhikkhu Pāsādika. He held posts at Kyushu University, serving as an associate professor (attested 2002) and later as a professor of Indian philosophy (attested 2013–2026).

Kiyoshi Shimokawabe is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at Rissho University. He held positions at Rissho University (attested 1990 and 2001) and the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra (attested 2001).

Kiyoshi Yabuuchi was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Sinology who studied at Kyoto University from roughly 1926 to 1929. He later held posts at Kyoto University from around 1935 to 1969 and Ryukoku University from roughly 1969 to 1979.

Kiyotaka Kimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Sinology who earned a doctorate at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (1983–2001) and served as president of Tsurumi Women's University (~2000–2012).

Kiyotaka Yoshimizu is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and under Gerhard Oberhammer. He held academic positions at Hokkaido University (~1993–2004), Tohoku University (~2004–2019), and Toyo Bunko.

Kiyozo Kazama is a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji and Harushige Kōzu, and at the University of Vienna. He held positions at Nagoya University, the University of Tokyo, and Hosei University.

Klaus Bruhn was an Indologist who studied under Walther Schubring and Ludwig Alsdorf at the University of Hamburg. He served as professor of Indology and Indian philology at the Free University of Berlin from 1966 to 1991/1993.

Klaus Butzenberger is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Friedrich Wilhelm at the University of Munich. He held posts at the Free University of Berlin and served as chairholder at the University of Tübingen from 1999 to 2017.

Klaus Karttunen is an Indology, linguistics, and history scholar who studied at the University of Helsinki under Pentti Aalto and Asko Parpola. He held research and docent positions at the Academy of Finland and the University of Helsinki.

Klaus Ludwig Janert was an Indologist who completed his doctoral studies under Paul Thieme and habilitated at the University of Tübingen. He worked as an assistant at the University of Göttingen before holding a full professorship at the University of Cologne (1963–1987).

Klaus Mylius was an Indologist and linguist who earned his doctorate at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg and habilitated at the University of Leipzig. He held teaching posts at Leipzig (1970–1991) and Goethe University Frankfurt (1996–2022).
Klaus Pinte is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and Sinology. He studied at Ghent University under Pol Vanden Broucke and held a postdoctoral teaching staff position there in 2006.

Klaus Röhrborn is a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and Buddhist studies and linguistics who studied under Bertold Spuler, Wolfgang Lentz, and Annemarie von Gabain. He was a professor at the University of Giessen and the University of Göttingen (1992–2003).
Klaus Rüping is an Indologist who studied under Paul Hacker and held an academic post as a lecturer at the University of Münster (attested 1978).

Klaus Wille is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He has worked as a researcher at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2000–2009 and 2018–2026) and cataloged manuscripts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (attested 1997).

Klaus-Dieter Mathes is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Marburg under Michael Hahn and habilitated at the University of Hamburg, later serving as a professor at the University of Vienna.
